name: manual_c0f079
claim: When a spec says a digest uses 'the manifest encoding rules' (or similar), search the codebase for the spec's own vocabulary and reuse that function instead of borrowing a convention from a nearby file. In oramasys it is compat/manifest.py canonical_digest: sort_keys, compact separators (',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False, UTF-8, SHA-256. Default json.dumps separators give different bytes and break cross-request comparisons. Determinism and format tests cannot detect that difference, so pin the convention with a known-answer test when byte-identical encoding matters.

decisions.notes: oramasys#63 binding_digest, 2026-10-18. My brief to the subagent cited a _fingerprint helper in another module as the existing convention; the subagent reported that file did not exist in that checkout and found canonical_digest in manifest.py, the literal match for the spec's phrase. I corrected the encoding before integration; the 26 tests passed either way, so they would not have caught it. A brief's premise is itself a claim to verify (the pushback was right). A known-answer test for the digest was not added in this pass and is recorded as a follow-up.
